newsitem.title: UK: London freight - US Gulf Panamaxes weaken.
newsitem.headline: London freight - US Gulf Panamaxes weaken.

text.p: Negative influences predominated in the dry cargo freight market on Wednesday with significantly weaker rates reported for Panamaxes from US Gulf and S Africa.

The BFI was down 13 points to 1475. But brokers reported a good volume of fresh enquiry for Panamax grain and fertilizer shipments from US Gulf to the Far East for first half December. Caper rates were generally no better than steady, and activity in the Handy-sizes was limited, especially in the grain trades.

Tradigrain fixed and failed on subjects with Tigris for about 78,000 barley Continent/Jeddah at a firm $17.75. But otherwise some Atlantic grain rates appeared weaker. Tuesday's rumours that Dreyfus covered 56,000 lights Mississippi/Holland-Belgium for end Nov at a lumpsum equivalent of $13.60 were confirmed with the fixture of the 3,060,000 cft Orjen. This compares unfavourably with Cobelfret's fixture 10 days ago of Diavolezza for 59,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Hamburg for Dec 1/10 at $14.10.

On the other hand brokers reported fresh first half December Panamax grain enquiry from First Steamship to Japan, Dreyfus and Hanjin to Malaysia, and Daiichi to Singapore-Japan range. In the Pacific Angelic Faith 65,772 dwt was closely trading NSAC delivery prompt Kashima for a trip via PNW to Taiwan at $12,000 daily but space 69,041 dwt intervened and is reported to have fixed the business delivery Nopac early Dec at $12,200 daily plus $210,000 bonus.

Reports circulated that Casinomar booked an 80,000 dwt vessel delivery Philippines in December for 12 months at $9,500 daily. D'Amato were linked with a 1978-built 64,000 dwt vessel delivery Continent for the same period at between $7,500 and 8,000 daily. There were few reports of Handy-size grain fixtures in the Atlantic but brokers reported more enquiry from Australia from charterers such as Glencore, Meezan and the Wheat Board. OML fixed a Japanese Food Agency cargo on timecharter on a 23,500 dwt vessel from NoPac to Japan at just below $6,000 daily plus $100,000 bonus.

Olivia 157,000 dwt was believed fixed from Las Palmas via Brazil with ironore to Constanza, Navalis 133,000 dwt from China to the Atlantic, and Golden Cape 123,043 dwt by Grant on subjects for 120,000 ironore Goa/Constanza for Dec 1/15, but further details were lacking. Yukong are said to have failed with Giovanni Grimaldi 135,000 dwdelivery mid Dec for 2 laden legs in the Atlantic. Preag fixed a Panamax for 60,000 coal Richards Bay/Rotterdam for Dec 15/30 at a surprisingly low $8.50, and Cargill quoted a new order for 60-65,000 tonnes Maracaibo/Ijmuiden for Dec 6/13.

Armada were said to have fixed Alfios 64,000 dwt delivery Morocco for 2 laden legs Atlantic business on private terms. In the East Northern Light was believed to have fixed ironore from W Australia to China. Daiichi were reported to have chartered a 69,000 dwt vessel delivery Japan for a Kalimantan round at only $10,300 daily. Fertilizer charterers quoted a number of chartering enquiries for Panamaxes in the Atlantic - for example United Interocean, Seyang and Klaveness for Tampa/China Nov/Dec, Dec 3/10 and 10/25 respectively, and Transfield for any Dec, and Bulfracht for Ventspils/China for early Dec.

Helen B 70,537 dwt has been fixed by Noble for end Nov delivery US Gulf with fertilizers to China on private terms. Koula l 71,730wt is believed fixed by Gesuri Lloyd delivery Aqaba trip Indonesia at about $11,000 daily. Bulknova have taken the 1977-built Rex Friendship 61,271 dwt delivery passing Muscat end Nov for 5-7 months at a firm $10,700 daily.

Van Ommeren fixed Baltic Bulker 27,586 dwt delivery prompt Continent trip USEC/Gulf at just below $8,000 daily and reports surfaced of Elikon 28,234 dwt fixed last week by the same charterers delivery Venezuela for 2-4 months at close to $6,600 daily. In the Far East Canpotex were rumoured to have fixed the 1972-built Heron 34,914 dwt delivery NoPac for 3-5 months at $7,500/7,750 daily plus $140,000 bonus. Star booked box-hold 26,000 dwt craned bulker from Singapore to the Arabian gulf at $7,250 daily.
